section_summary: This section concerns proposed ship construction in occupied Japan, the return of Japanese merchant ships to overseas trade, and requests for access to foreign ports. It also records Japanese appointments to measure vessels for canal tonnage certificates and diplomatic efforts to recover Japanese fishing boats seized by Chinese forces.

subfiles.title: Conroy inquiry to the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conroy asks whether law restricts a proposed Japanese-built vessel transaction.
subfiles.summary: Encloses his inquiry to the Maritime Commission and its reply, and requests State Department advice.

subfiles.title: Maritime Commission reply to Conroy
subfiles.from: Ruth Holmes, United States Maritime Commission
subfiles.about: The Commission addresses its jurisdiction over a Japanese-built vessel sold for Portuguese registry.
subfiles.summary: Says the Commission lacks jurisdiction over such peacetime transactions and suggests consulting the State Department.

subfiles.title: Conroy inquiry to the Maritime Commission
subfiles.about: A New York corporation proposes to build an 1,800-ton steamer in Japan for resale under the Portuguese flag.
subfiles.summary: Asks whether occupation rules or law prevent construction and resale without placing the vessel under the American flag.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Conroy
subfiles.from: Edward W. Doherty, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department explains United States law and occupation authority relevant to Conroy's proposed transaction.
subfiles.summary: The Department knows of no United States legal bar to foreign construction and direct Portuguese registry. It explains that business in Japan must comply with Japanese and SCAP rules and recommends consulting SCAP headquarters.

subfiles.title: Smokeless Fuel Company inquiry on Japanese shipping
subfiles.to: Office of the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The company seeks information on Japanese shipping permissions and licensed companies.
subfiles.summary: Its London representatives want a contact and shipping-company list to pursue bunker fuel and agency business.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram on Japanese merchant marine
subfiles.about: Transmits a SCAP assessment of Japanese merchant tonnage, trade routes, and foreign-exchange savings.
subfiles.summary: Reports that new construction will take months and that existing and converted tonnage will support overseas trade, chiefly with Asian countries. It revises estimates of freight savings and earnings, discusses the limited effect of opening United States ports, and notes that Japanese vessels are not yet providing liner service.

subfiles.title: Taipei telegram on seized Japanese fishing vessels
subfiles.to: Secretary of State and listed United States military recipients
subfiles.about: Reports Chinese naval use of seized Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: Says the vessels are dispersed around Taiwan and used for smuggling, fishing, and coastal patrols.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram requesting port clearances for Japanese vessels
subfiles.about: SCAP seeks blanket clearance and equal treatment for Japanese cargo vessels entering foreign ports.
subfiles.summary: Individual clearance requests are too slow for planned overseas trade. The mission asks the Department to approach listed governments as Japanese ocean-going tonnage expands.

subfiles.title: Appointment of admeasurers by Japanese Government
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Japan appoints seven men to certify vessel tonnage for passage through the Panama and Suez canals.
subfiles.summary: Reports that canal authorities and interested diplomatic missions received the list of appointees.

subfiles.title: List of Japanese government admeasurers
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Lists seven appointees and their training and current offices.
subfiles.summary: Names seven naval architects appointed to measure vessel tonnage for Panama and Suez canal certificates.

subfiles.title: Taipei report on efforts to recover fishing vessels
subfiles.from: Donald D. Edgar, American Consul, Taipei
subfiles.about: Reports approaches to Taiwan authorities concerning seized Japanese fishing vessels.
subfiles.summary: General Chen Cheng promises to investigate; Admiral Kwei says the Chinese Navy needs several captured vessels for military operations.

subfiles.title: Taipei telegram on approach to Foreign Minister Yeh
subfiles.about: Describes a diplomatic request to end seizures and return Japanese fishing vessels and crews.
subfiles.summary: Yeh condemns the seizures and indicates agreement that SCAP governs Japanese vessels on the high seas, while reserving Chinese rights in territorial waters. He does not commit to returning the vessels or crews. The embassy requests details of Japanese inspection craft and will press for a reply.
